newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Airlines ups Srinagar cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: Indian Airlines ups Srinagar cargo capacity.

text.p: Indian Airlines (IA) will next month increase its total daily inbound/outbound Srinagar cargo capacity to around five tonnes from the existing 2.5 tonnes, the carrier's station manager said.
It will fly a daily Airbus A300 from April 1, in addition to the existing Airbus A320 which flies direct from Delhi on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
Cargo demand has increased slowly for the first time in seven years following the elections held in Kashmir last year, he added.
There is also a daily Boeing 737 IA Delhi-Jammu-Srinagar flight.

Private airline Jet Airways flies into Srinagar with a Boeing 737 but is not allowed to move cargo as they do not have cargo X-ray facilities or the infrastructure for handling cargo, the airport manager said.
IA installed its X-ray machine a year ago in the cargo area which has a capacity of 40 tonnes, but no cold area.

An Express Cargo service has been started by IA and will take consignments up to three hours before flight departures. All incoming cargo can be cleared the same day and cargo despatch is normally within 24 hours of its arrival at Srinagar for onward air despatch.
As for onward export cargo, the manager said it is normally moved through Indian Airlines and then either via Lufthansa Cargo,, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV,, Air India or British Airways Plc.
Although detailed figures were not available, woollen and silk carpets now represented about five percent of total exports with most going to Germany and the U.S.
Carpet industry sources said the export market was still not as good as it was 10 years ago and was facing stiff competition in Europe from lower quality, but cheaper Chinese carpets.
The market was also down for leather exports which were now crafted more in New Delhi than Srinagar, with Russian buyers shipping large amounts, from warehouses they had set up in Delhi.

One carpet manufacturer here said that for consignments up to 300kg, he used air. But over that weight, transport by road was cheaper and his preferred route. The Delhi-Srinagar-Delhi air rate is 20 rupees for under one kg.
The rate then falls to 16.50 rupees per kg. There is a special Srinagar-Delhi rate of 7.45 rupees per kg for flowers, fruit and vegetables with a minimum load of 45kg.
Other potential products for air cargo are summer apples, cherries, mushrooms, cardamom, saffron, and handicrafts.
